title: Finite powers commute with forming complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and $d\in\mathbf N$. The finite categorical power functor $M\mapsto\prod_{i<d}M$ is additive, preserves every existing shape of limits, and preserves finite colimits. Applying it degreewise to a cochain complex $P$ gives a natural isomorphism to $\prod_{i<d}P$. Its $i$th projection in degree $k$ is the ordinary $i$th projection of $\prod_{i<d}P^k$. This includes the empty power $d=0$.

proof.text: Identify finite power with the constant diagram functor followed by the limit functor on Discrete (Fin d). The constant functor preserves limits and colimits; finite limits in an abelian category are exact for discrete finite shapes by biproducts. Thus finite power is additive and preserves limits and finite colimits.

Lift the degreewise coordinate projections to a chain map from the degreewise product complex into the categorical product. Evaluating in any degree and composing with the product comparison is the identity by product extensionality. Both this comparison and hence the evaluated chain map are isomorphisms. Componentwise isomorphisms give a complex isomorphism. Projection and naturality follow by product extensionality.
